questions.question: Explain the concept of urban governance.
questions.solution_html:
• Migration as a Cause of Urban Social Disorganisation
  • a) Rapid population growth- Influx of migrants leads to overcrowding in cities.
  • b) Housing shortages and slums- Migrants often settle in informal settlements with poor conditions.
  • c) Pressure on urban infrastructure- Overburdened water supply, sanitation, transport, and
  • healthcare systems.
  • d) Unemployment and informal sector growth- Limited job opportunities push migrants into
  • insecure work.
  • e) Cultural heterogeneity- Diverse backgrounds may lead to cultural clashes and weak social
  • cohesion.
  • f) Weak social control- Absence of strong community bonds increases deviant behaviour.
  • Urban Social Disorganisation Affecting Migrants
  • a) Social exclusion and marginalization- Migrants face discrimination and lack of integration.
  • b) Poor living conditions- Slums lack basic amenities, affecting health and dignity.
  • c) Crime and insecurity- Disorganised environments often see higher crime rates.
  • d) Family disintegration- Migration may separate families or create stress within them.
  • e) Limited access to services- Education, healthcare, and welfare services are often inaccessible.
  • Interrelationship (Two-way Process)
  • a) Cycle of poverty- Migration leads to urban poverty, which reinforces disorganisation.
  • b) Mutual reinforcement- Disorganisation attracts vulnerable migrants and worsens conditions.
  • c) Strain on governance- Urban institutions struggle to manage growing populations.
  • d) Impact on sustainable development- Unplanned growth undermines long-term urban stability. .
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: Migration as a Cause of Urban Social Disorganisation

questions.question: Analyse the concept, scope and indicators of Community Development. (, An)
questions.solution_html:
• Examine the role of trusteeship and decentralization in Gandhian rural development.
  • (Trusteeship in Gandhian Rural Development
  • a) Concept of trusteeship- Wealthy individuals should act as trustees of their wealth for the welfare
  • of society.
  • b) Reduction of inequality- Promotes equitable distribution of resources without violent conflict.
  • c) Moral responsibility- Emphasizes ethical use of wealth and social accountability.
  • d) Non-exploitative economy- Discourages exploitation of labour and resources.
  • e) Voluntary sharing -Encourages voluntary redistribution rather than forced confiscation.
  • f) Class harmony- Aims to reduce conflict between rich and poor.
  • g) Focus on social welfare- Prioritizes community well-being over individual profit.
  • Decentralization in Gandhian Rural Development
  • a) Gram Swaraj (village self-rule)- Villages function as self-sufficient units of governance.
  • b) Local self-governance-Power is vested in village institutions like Panchayats.
  • c) People’s participation - Encourages active involvement of citizens in decision-making.
  • d) Efficient resource utilization- Local resources are used based on local needs.
  • e) Transparency and accountability- Decision-making at the grassroots ensures better
  • accountability.
  • f) Reduction of bureaucratic control- Limits over-centralization and delays.
  • g) Promotion of self-reliance- Villages become economically and socially independent.
  • Combined Role in Rural Development
  •  Together, trusteeship and decentralization promote equity, participation, sustainability, and
  • inclusive development, forming the foundation of Gandhian rural reconstruction.

questions.question: Examine the interrelationship between migration and urban social disorganisation.
questions.solution_html:
• a) Rapid population growth- Influx of migrants leads to overcrowding in cities.
  • b) Housing shortages and slums- Migrants often settle in informal settlements with poor conditions.
  • c) Pressure on urban infrastructure- Overburdened water supply, sanitation, transport, and
  • healthcare systems.
  • d) Unemployment and informal sector growth- Limited job opportunities push migrants into
  • insecure work.
  • e) Cultural heterogeneity- Diverse backgrounds may lead to cultural clashes and weak social
  • cohesion.
  • f) Weak social control- Absence of strong community bonds increases deviant behaviour.
  • Urban Social Disorganisation Affecting Migrants
  • a) Social exclusion and marginalization- Migrants face discrimination and lack of integration.
  • b) Poor living conditions- Slums lack basic amenities, affecting health and dignity.
  • c) Crime and insecurity- Disorganised environments often see higher crime rates.
  • d) Family disintegration- Migration may separate families or create stress within them.
  • e) Limited access to services- Education, healthcare, and welfare services are often inaccessible.
  • Interrelationship (Two-way Process)
  • a) Cycle of poverty- Migration leads to urban poverty, which reinforces disorganisation.
  • b) Mutual reinforcement- Disorganisation attracts vulnerable migrants and worsens conditions.
  • c) Strain on governance- Urban institutions struggle to manage growing populations.
  • d) Impact on sustainable development- Unplanned growth undermines long-term urban stability. .
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: Migration as a Cause of Urban Social Disorganisation

questions.question: Estimate the effectiveness of livelihood promotion strategies in enhancing rural income.
questions.solution_html:
• a) Income generation opportunities- Provide sustainable sources of income through self
  • employment and wage employment.
  • b) Diversification of livelihoods- Reduce dependence on agriculture by promoting non-farm
  • activities like small enterprises and services.
  • c) Skill development and capacity building- Training programmes enhance employability and
  • productivity.
  • d) Promotion of micro-enterprises- Encourages rural entrepreneurship and local economic growth.
  • e) Access to credit and financial inclusion- Microfinance and banking services help the poor invest
  • in income-generating activities.
  • f) Strengthening Self-Help Groups (SHGs)- SHGs promote savings, credit access, and collective
  • economic activities.
  • g) Women empowerment- Increases women’s participation in economic activities and decision
  • making.
  • h) Improved market linkages- Better access to markets helps in getting fair prices for products.
  • i) Reduction in poverty levels- Increased income contributes to better living standards.
  • j) Employment generation- Reduces unemployment and underemployment in rural areas.
  • Limitations and Challenges
  • a) Unequal access to benefits- Marginalized groups may not fully benefit.
  • b) Lack of awareness and training- Beneficiaries may not utilize opportunities effectively.
  • c) Market constraints- Poor infrastructure and weak demand limit income growth.
  • d) Implementation gaps-Inefficiency and corruption reduce programme impact.
  • e) Sustainability issues- Some initiatives fail without continuous support.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: Estimate the effectiveness of livelihood promotion strategies in enhancing rural income
